title: Media & News
description: Discuss TV, radio, newspapers, social media, and current events using relative pronouns, passive se, past subjunctive for hypothetical scenarios, and object pronouns for media consumption.

grammar.title: Relative Pronouns — que, quien, el cual, donde
grammar.content:
Relative pronouns connect ideas and describe people, things, and places. They are essential for discussing media and news.

Basic relative pronouns:

1. QUE — the most common relative pronoun, refers to people and things
   - El noticiero que veo es interesante. (The news program I watch is interesting.)
   - La película que vimos fue emocionante. (The movie we watched was exciting.)

2. QUIEN / QUIENES — refers to people (with or without preposition)
   - El periodista que me entrevistó fue muy amable. (The journalist who interviewed me was very kind.)
   - La persona a quien llamaste no está. (The person you called is not here.)

3. EL CUAL / LA CUAL / LOS CUALES / LAS CUALES — more formal than 'que', used after prepositions
   - El artículo, el cual fue publicado ayer, es muy importante. (The article, which was published yesterday, is very important.)
   - La serie, de la cual hablaste, ¿dónde la puedo ver? (The series you talked about, where can I watch it?)

4. DONDE — refers to places
   - El canal donde se emiten las noticias es el 5. (The channel where the news is broadcast is channel 5.)

5. LO QUE — 'that which / what', refers to an idea or situation
   - Lo que quiero es una buena noticia. (What I want is good news.)
   - Lo que dijeron en la radio es verdad. (What they said on the radio is true.)

Prepositions + relative pronouns (for people):
   - con quien (with whom)
   - para quien (for whom)
   - sobre quien (about whom)
   - de quien (of whom / about whom)

Examples:
- El periódico que leí ayer tenía muchas noticias. (The newspaper I read yesterday had many news stories.)
- La serie en la que estoy es muy divertida. (The series I'm watching is very funny.)
- Lo que más me gusta de Internet es la información. (What I like most about the Internet is the information.)
- El presentador con quien hablaron fue muy profesional. (The presenter they spoke with was very professional.)
examples: El noticiero que miro todos los días es del canal 8. (The news program I watch every day is from channel 8.)
La persona que publicó el artículo es mi amiga. (The person who published the article is my friend.)
Lo que escuché en la radio me sorprendió. (What I heard on the radio surprised me.)
El programa donde entrevistan al presidente es muy popular. (The program where they interview the president is very popular.)
Los documentos de los que hablamos son confidenciales. (The documents we talked about are confidential.)
La serie a la que me suscribí acaba de terminar. (The series I subscribed to has just ended.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian has relative pronouns too, but they are different: 'care' (which/that), 'carei/carele' (more emphatic), 'cui' (to whom), 'unde' (where). The Spanish 'que' is the closest to Romanian 'care.' Romanian 'ceea ce' = Spanish 'lo que.' Key difference: Spanish 'que' works for both things AND people, while Romanian 'care' is for things and 'cui' is for people. For Romanian speakers: 'que' is your go-to relative pronoun — use it 90% of the time.

grammar.title: Passive 'se' — Talking About What Happens in the World
grammar.content:
The passive 'se' (also called 'se impersonal' or 'se pasiva') is used to describe what happens in general or what is done to things — very common in news and media contexts.

Formation: se + verb (3rd person singular or plural) + subject

When the subject is SINGULAR:
  se + verb (3rd person singular)
  - Se vende la casa. (The house is being sold.)
  - Se transmite el partido en vivo. (The match is broadcast live.)
  - Se publica la noticia en el periódico. (The news is published in the newspaper.)

When the subject is PLURAL:
  se + verb (3rd person plural)
  - Se venden casas. (Houses are being sold.)
  - Se transmiten partidos en vivo. (Matches are broadcast live.)
  - Se publican noticias todos los días. (News is published every day.)

Key rules:
1. The verb agrees with the subject in number (singular/plural)
2. No person is mentioned — this is the whole point (who does it is unimportant)
3. Very common in news headlines and everyday speech

Media examples:
- Se emiten documentales sobre la naturaleza. (Documentaries about nature are broadcast.)
- Se publica una nueva serie este viernes. (A new series is published this Friday.)
- Se transmiten las noticias a las ocho. (The news is broadcast at eight.)
- Se filma un documental en la selva. (A documentary is filmed in the jungle.)

Contrast with 'se' impersonal (no subject, always singular):
- Se vive bien aquí. (One lives well here.)
- Se dice que va a llover. (They say it's going to rain.)
- Se necesita más información. (More information is needed.)

Examples:
- En este canal se emiten programas de cultura. (On this channel, culture programs are broadcast.)
- Se publican artículos sobre política cada día. (Articles about politics are published every day.)
- Se filmó una película en nuestro pueblo. (A movie was filmed in our town.)
- Se necesitan voluntarios para el evento. (Volunteers are needed for the event.)
examples: Se transmite un documental sobre el cambio climático esta noche. (A documentary about climate change is being broadcast tonight.)
Se publican nuevas series todos los meses. (New series are published every month.)
Se puede ver la película en streaming. (The movie can be watched via streaming.)
Se reportaron muchos accidentes en la carretera. (Many accidents were reported on the highway.)
Se emiten noticias en vivo durante las elecciones. (News is broadcast live during elections.)
Se filman documentales sobre la fauna marina. (Documentaries about marine wildlife are filmed.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses 'se' in a similar way: 'se spune' (they say), 'se transmite' (it is broadcast). However, Romanian also has a full passive construction with 'fi' (este vândut = is being sold). Spanish passive 'se' is much more common and covers both impersonal and passive meanings. For Romanian speakers: when you'd say 'este vândut' or 'se vinde' in Romanian, Spanish uses 'se vende.' The pattern is very similar — just remember the verb must agree with the subject in number.

grammar.title: Past Subjunctive for Hypothetical Media Scenarios
grammar.content:
The imperfect subjunctive is used to talk about hypothetical or unreal situations involving media, news, and entertainment.

Formation (two forms, both correct):
-RA form: take 3rd person plural of preterite, remove -ron, add endings
  hablar → hablaran → hablara, hablaras, hablara, habláramos, hablarais, hablaran
-SE form: same stem, add -se endings
  hablar → hablase, hablases, hablase, hablásemos, hablarais, hablasen

Irregulars in preterite 3rd pl.:
  ser/ir → fueron → fuera/fuese
  tener → tuvieran → tuviera/tuviese
  hacer → hicieron → hiciera/hiciese
  poder → pudieron → pudiera/pudiese
  querer → quisieron → quisiera/quisiese
  saber → supieron → supiera/supiese
  decir → dijeron → dijera/dijese
  venir → vinieron → viniera/viniese

Uses in media contexts:

1. SI clauses (unreal present): Si tuviera un canal de TV, emitiera noticias. (If I had a TV channel, I would broadcast news.)
   Note: si clause uses subjunctive, main clause uses conditional

2. WISHES and HOPES about media: Ojalá hubieran publicado la noticia. (I wish they had published the news.)

3. AFTER PAST expressions of desire/doubt/emotion:
   Quería que publicaran más artículos. (I wanted them to publish more articles.)
   Dudaba que existiera tal noticia. (I doubted that such a news item existed.)

4. POLITE REQUESTS:
   Quisiera ver esa película. (I would like to see that movie.)
   Preferiría que no lo transmitieran. (I would prefer that they not broadcast it.)

Media examples:
- Si yo fuera periodista, escribiría sobre la cultura. (If I were a journalist, I would write about culture.)
- Quisiera que subieran más videos a mi canal. (I would like them to upload more videos to my channel.)
- Era imposible que alguien creyera esas noticias falsas. (It was impossible that someone believed those fake news.)
- Si el presentador hubiera hablado más claro, todos habrían entendido. (If the presenter had spoken more clearly, everyone would have understood.)
examples: Si tuviera Internet, vería la transmisión en vivo. (If I had Internet, I would watch the live stream.)
Quisiera que publicaran mi artículo. (I would like them to publish my article.)
Era una pena que no se emitiera el programa. (It was a shame that the program wasn't broadcast.)
Si la película fuera aburrida, no la compartiría. (If the movie were boring, I wouldn't share it.)
Dudaba que la noticia fuera verdadera. (I doubted that the news was true.)
Ojalá hubiera visto esa serie antes. (I wish I had seen that series before.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian uses 'ar + infinitive' for conditional ('aș vedea' = I would watch) and 'să + present/imperfect' for subjunctive ('să vedeam' = that I might see). Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive (-ra/-se forms) where Romanian would use the imperfect subjunctive with 'să.' For Romanian speakers: 'Si yo fuera periodista' = 'Dacă aș fi jurnalist' — both use a conditional-like form in the si/si clause. The key pattern is: SI + imperfect subjunctive → conditional in the main clause.

grammar.title: Object Pronouns with Media Actions
grammar.content:
Object pronouns (direct and indirect) replace nouns to avoid repetition when talking about media consumption, sharing, and communication.

Direct Object Pronouns (what/whom is acted upon):
  lo / la (him/her/it — masc./fem. sg.)
  los / las (them — masc./fem. pl.)
  Examples:
  - ¿Viste la película? Sí, la vi. (Did you see the movie? Yes, I saw it.)
  - ¿Escuchaste el podcast? No, no lo escuché. (Did you listen to the podcast? No, I didn't listen to it.)

Indirect Object Pronouns (to/for whom):
  me (to me) / te (to you) / le (to him/her/you formal)
  nos (to us) / os (to you all) / les (to them/you all)
  Examples:
  - ¿Le enviaste el mensaje? Sí, se lo envié. (Did you send him the message? Yes, I sent it to him.)
  - ¿Me recomendaste esa serie? Sí, te la recomendé. (Did you recommend that series to me? Yes, I recommended it to you.)

Position of object pronouns:
  1. Before conjugated verb: La veo todos los días.
  2. Attached to infinitive: Voy a verla.
  3. Attached to gerund: Estoy viéndola.
  4. Attached to affirmative commands: ¡Véela!

Double object pronouns (indirect + direct):
  le/les + lo/la/los/las → se lo / se la / se los / se las
  - Le di el periódico → Se lo di. (I gave him the newspaper → I gave it to him.)
  - Les envié los videos → Se los envié. (I sent them the videos → I sent them to them.)

Media-specific examples:
  - ¿Viste las noticias de ayer? Sí, las vi. (Did you see yesterday's news? Yes, I saw them.)
  - ¿Compartiste el video? Sí, lo compartí. (Did you share the video? Yes, I shared it.)
  - ¿Le mostraste el artículo a tu amigo? Sí, se lo mostré. (Did you show him the article? Yes, I showed it to him.)
  - No la sigo en redes sociales. (I don't follow her on social media.)
  - Voy a suscribirme al podcast. → Lo voy a suscribir. (I'm going to subscribe to the podcast. → I'm going to subscribe to it.)
examples: ¿Viste la nueva serie? Sí, la vi el fin de semana. (Did you see the new series? Yes, I watched it on the weekend.)
No escuché el podcast. ¿Puedes enviármelo? (I didn't listen to the podcast. Can you send it to me?)
Les compartí las fotos del evento. (I shared the event photos with them.)
¿Me suscribíste al boletín? (Did you subscribe me to the newsletter?)
Voy a publicarlo en mi cuenta. (I'm going to post it on my account.)
Se la recomendé a mi hermano. (I recommended it to my brother.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian object pronouns: 'îl/îi' (masc. sg.), 'o/le' (fem. sg.), 'pe ei/pe ele' (emphasis). Romanian pronoun placement is BEFORE the conjugated verb (îl văd = I see it), similar to Spanish. The key differences: 1) Romanian doesn't attach pronouns to infinitives the same way (îl văd vs. a-l vedea — both exist but usage differs). 2) Spanish double object pronouns merge 'le lo' → 'se lo', which is unique to Spanish. For Romanian speakers: 'îl' (masc. it) ≈ 'lo', 'o/le' (fem. it/them) ≈ 'la/las', 'îi/le' (to him/to them) ≈ 'le/les.' The placement rule is the same — before the verb.

pronunciation.title: Media & News Pronunciation — Media Vocabulary and News Terms
pronunciation.content:
Clear pronunciation of media and news vocabulary helps you discuss current events and entertainment naturally.

Key pronunciation patterns:

1. Trailing '-ción' and '-sión' (stress on the 's' sound):
   - la noticia = no-TEE-see-ah (but 'noticias' = no-TEE-see-ahs)
   - la televisión = teh-leh-vee-ah-SEE-ohn
   - la información = in-for-mah-SEE-ohn
   - la decisión = deh-see-EE-ohn
   - la presión = preh-SEE-ohn
   Note: '-ción' sounds like 'see-OHN'

2. Trailing '-miento' (stress on 'mien'):
   - el entretenimiento = en-ter-teh-nee-MYEN-toh
   - el pensamiento = pen-see-MAHEN-toh
   - el sentimiento = sen-tee-MYEN-toh

3. 'ñ' (ny sound):
   - el año = AH-nyoh
   - la niña = NEE-nyah
   - la mañana = mah-NYAH-nah
   - el niño = NEE-nyoh

4. 'll' (y sound in most regions):
   - la lluvia = YOO-ah (rare, but good to know)
   - el pollo = PO-yoh
   - la calle = KAH-yeh

5. 'j' (soft g, like harsh 'h'):
   - la noticia = no-TEE-see-ah (no 'j' sound)
   - el periodista = her-nah-LEE-stah
   - justo = HOOS-toh
   - jugar = hoo-GAH
   - trabajo = tra-BAH-hoh

6. 'g' before 'e/i' (soft g, like harsh 'h'):
   - la televisión = teh-leh-vee-ah-see-OHN
   - el gobierno = go-BYER-noh
   - la gente = HEN-teh
   - el periodista = her-NAH-listah

7. 'v' and 'b' (both sound like soft 'b' in Spanish):
   - la televisión = teh-leh-vee-ah-see-OHN (v sounds like b)
   - el periodista = her-NAH-listah
   - ver = bair (v = soft b)
   - vida = BEE-dah

8. 'z' (s sound in Spain, 'th' in parts of Spain, 's' in Latin America):
   - la noticia = no-TEE-see-ah (Latin America)
   - el periodista = her-NAH-listah
   - la decisión = deh-see-EE-ohn

9. 'r' at beginning of word (rolled r):
   - radio = RAH-dio
   - reportaje = reh-por-TAH-heh
   - redacción = reh-DAK-see-ohn

10. Stress on '-al' endings:
    - el canal = kah-NAHL
    - el editorial = eh-dee-toh-REE-al
    - local = lo-KAHL
    - global = GLO-bal

Common media words — pronunciation guide:
- noticias = no-TEE-see-ahs (stress on 'TEE')
- televisión = teh-leh-vee-ah-see-OHN (stress on 'see-OHN')
- periódico = peh-ree-oh-DEE-koh (stress on 'DEE')
- periodista = her-NAH-listah (stress on 'NAH')
- programa = pro-GRA-mah (stress on 'GRA')
- entrevista = en-treh-VEES-tah (stress on 'VEES')
- documental = doh-koo-men-TAHL (stress on 'TAHL')
- podcast = pod-KAST (similar to English)
- publicar = poo-blee-KAH (stress on 'KAH')
- compartir = kom-par-TIR (stress on 'TIR')
- seguir = seh-GEER (stress on 'GEER')
- redacción = reh-DAK-see-ohn (stress on 'DAK')
- noticia = no-TEE-see-ah (stress on 'TEE')
- titular = too-tee-NAHL (stress on 'NAH')
- tendencia = ten-DEN-see-ah (stress on 'DEN')
- algoritmo = ah-l-go-REE-toh (stress on 'REE')
- transmisión = trahns-mee-SEE-ohn (stress on 'see-OHN')
- entretenimiento = en-ter-teh-nee-MYEN-toh (stress on 'MYEN')
examples: noticias = no-TEE-see-ahs (stress on 'TEE')
televisión = teh-leh-vee-ah-see-OHN (stress on 'see-OHN')
periodista = her-NAH-listah (stress on 'NAH')
documental = doh-koo-men-TAHL (stress on 'TAHL')
transmisión = trahns-mee-see-OHN (stress on 'see-OHN')
entretenimiento = en-ter-teh-nee-MYEN-toh (stress on 'MYEN')

exercises.question: What is the Spanish word for 'social media'?
exercises.explanation: 'Las redes sociales' means 'social media.' 'Redes' comes from 'red' (network). This is the standard term used in Spanish.

exercises.question: Which relative pronoun means 'who' when referring to a person?
exercises.explanation: 'Quien' refers to people. 'El cual' is more formal and used after prepositions. 'Donde' refers to places. 'Lo que' refers to ideas/situations.

exercises.question: Complete: 'La película ___ vimos fue increíble.' (The movie we watched was incredible.)
exercises.explanation: 'Que' is the most common relative pronoun for both people and things. 'La película que vimos' = The movie we watched.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the passive 'se' correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Se venden periódicos' is correct — the verb 'venden' is plural to agree with the plural subject 'periódicos.' 'Se vende' would be for singular: 'Se vende el periódico.'

exercises.question: Complete with the correct direct object pronoun: '¿Viste las noticias? Sí, ___ vi.'
exercises.explanation: 'Las noticias' is feminine plural, so the direct object pronoun is 'las.' 'Sí, las vi' = Yes, I saw them.

exercises.question: What does 'el titular' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'El titular' means 'the headline.' 'El escritor' = writer, 'el editor' = editor, 'el editor / el publicador' = publisher.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si yo ___ (tener) un canal de TV, emitiera noticias.'
exercises.explanation: 'Si' + imperfect subjunctive for hypothetical: 'tuviera' (from tener). 'Si yo tuviera un canal de TV' = If I had a TV channel.

exercises.question: What does 'se transmite el partido en vivo' mean?
options: They are watching the match live.
exercises.explanation: 'Se transmite' = is broadcast (passive se, present tense). 'En vivo' = live. 'El partido' = the match. The full sentence = The match is broadcast live.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct object pronoun: '¿Me recomendaste la serie? Sí, te ___ recomendé.'
exercises.explanation: 'La serie' is feminine singular, so the direct object pronoun is 'la.' 'Sí, te la recomendé' = Yes, I recommended it to you.

exercises.question: What does 'hoy en día' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Hoy en día' is an idiom meaning 'these days' or 'nowadays.' It's used to talk about current conditions.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct relative pronoun: 'Lo ___ quiero es ver una buena película.' (What I want is to watch a good movie.)
exercises.explanation: 'Lo que' = 'that which / what.' 'Lo que quiero' = 'What I want.' This construction refers to an idea, not a specific noun.

exercises.question: Which word means 'to broadcast' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Emitir' means 'to broadcast.' 'Grabar' = to record, 'descargar' = to download, 'publicar' = to publish/post.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Los artículos ___ leí fueron muy interesantes.' (The articles I read were very interesting.)
exercises.explanation: 'Que' is the relative pronoun for things. 'Los artículos que leí' = The articles I read. (Note: could also be 'en los que' in more formal usage.)

exercises.question: What does 'las falsas noticias' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Las falsas noticias' means 'fake news.' 'Falsas' = fake/false, 'noticias' = news. This is the term used for misinformation.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct indirect object pronoun: '___ envié el mensaje a mi amigo.' (I sent him the message.)
exercises.explanation: 'Le' is the third-person singular indirect object pronoun — 'to him.' 'Le envié el mensaje a mi amigo' = I sent him the message.

exercises.question: Which is the Spanish word for 'podcast'?
exercises.explanation: 'El podcast' is used directly in Spanish. It's a loanword from English, just like in many other languages.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si el periodista ___ (ser) más claro, todos habrían entendido.'
exercises.explanation: This is a past unreal condition: 'Si' + past perfect subjunctive → would have + past participle. 'Si el periodista hubiera sido más claro' = If the journalist had been clearer.

exercises.question: What does 'la redacción' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La redacción' means 'the newsroom' or 'editorial office.' It comes from 'redactar' (to draft/write an article).

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Se ___ (emitir) las noticias a las ocho?' (Is the news broadcast at eight?)
exercises.explanation: 'Las noticias' is plural, so the verb must be plural: 'se emiten.' '¿Se emiten las noticias a las ocho?' = Is the news broadcast at eight? (Note: could also accept 'emite' if referring to 'la noticia' singular.)

exercises.question: What does 'virar en redes' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Virar (en redes)' means 'to go viral' on social media. It's a colloquial expression derived from 'viral.'
